newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira to granulate coagulant for new mkts.
newsitem.headline: Kemira to granulate coagulant for new mkts.

text.p: Finnish chemicals and fertiliser group Kemira Oy said on Wednesday it would invest 25 million markka to start granulating polyaluminium chloride, which would widen its potential export markets for the chemical.
Polyaluminium chloride, used as a coagulant in water purification, is normally delivered as a solution, which costs more to transport, it said in a statement.
"Production of a dry solid permits more distant export, for example to potential markets such as Thailand, Africa and the Middle East," it said.
A spokesman at Kemira's plant in Helsingborg, Sweden, where the investment is planned, said Kemira's current capacity of polyaluminium chloride was 50,000 tonnes.
This would rise to over 70,000 tonnes, 20,000 of which would be for the new solid product, he said.
